title: Multimodal Crystal Flow: Any-to-Any Modality Generation for Unified Crystal Modeling
claim: Different generation tasks are just different paths through a two-time-variable space, so one model can cover them all.
layout: 2 panels: left time-axis square diagram, right three trajectory rows; arrows left-to-right
description: The left panel shows a square diagram. Its horizontal axis is atom-type time t and its vertical axis is structure time s. The corners are marked with black dots. Each corner has a 3D crystal cell. The bottom-left corner shows gray atoms packed in a flat, unstructured arrangement. The top-left corner shows gray atoms in a cell. The top-right and bottom-right corners show the final colored crystal, with green and red atoms. Three colored arrows mark the tasks. An orange arrow along the top is atom type generation. A blue arrow up the right side is crystal structure prediction. A green diagonal is de novo generation. Gray dashed axes frame the square. The right panel has three rows of four crystal snapshots. Each row has a matching colored arrow. It runs from the start condition, such as t=1,s=0, t=0,s=1 or t=s=0, to t=s=1. The rows show how each task's atoms gradually become colored and ordered. The colored arrows draw the eye first.
caption: Overview of multimodal crystal flow with any-to-any modality generation. MCFlow trains a flow model with two independent time variables corresponding to atom types ($t$) and structures ($s$). By selecting task-specific inference trajectories in the $(t,s)$ space, a single model performs crystal structure prediction, atom type generation, and de novo generation.
abstract: Crystal modeling spans a family of conditional and unconditional generation tasks, including crystal structure prediction (CSP) and de novo generation (DNG). While recent deep generative models have shown promising performance, they remain largely task-specific, lacking a unified framework that shares crystal representations across tasks. To address this limitation, we propose Multimodal Crystal Flow (MCFlow), a unified multimodal flow model that realizes multiple crystal generation tasks as distinct inference trajectories via independent time variables for atom types and crystal structures. To enable multimodal flow in a standard transformer model, we introduce a composition- and symmetry-aware atom ordering with hierarchical permutation augmentation, injecting compositional and crystallographic priors without explicit structural templates. Experiments on the MP-20 and MPTS-52 benchmarks show that a single MCFlow model is competitive with task-specific baselines across CSP, DNG, and structure-conditioned atom type generation.
